summary.headline: Sugs Lloyd Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR78.4 crore with EBITDA margin 15.3%; order book INR807 crore; FY28 INR1,000 crore target reaffirmed.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR78.40 crore, up 32% YoY, with EBITDA of about INR12 crore (15.3% margin, up 32 bps) and PAT of INR7.5 crore (up 30%). Management attributed the slower quarter to Patna project teething issues and supplier material shortages that pushed some June billing into Q2. Order book stood at INR807 crore (ex-GST) as of 30 June, and management reaffirmed the INR600 crore FY27 and INR1,000 crore FY28 revenue targets. Receivables fell by about INR10 crore to INR149 crore, while borrowings rose from INR68 crore to INR91 crore to fund Patna working capital.

segments.name: Power transmission, distribution and smart grid (incl. FPI)
segments.commentary: INR46.32 crore in Q1, ~59% of revenue. Fault passage indicator (FPI) is described as the fastest-growing niche, with >50% domestic share; Q1 FPI order wins already exceed the full FY26 product order value per management.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: INR32 crore in Q1, ~41% of revenue. Shifting toward RESCO and capex-plus-RESCO mandates with 10-year service contracts; first such order is Bihar PM-Surya Ghar at INR56 crore.

segments.name: Products / other (target)
segments.commentary: Management targets products at ~10% of revenue by FY28. No product revenue split disclosed for Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR600 crore reiterated as on track; Q1 slippage expected to be recovered in Q2.
FY28 revenue target of INR1,000 crore reaffirmed; management says it needs unexecuted order book of INR2,000-2,500 crore to deliver it.
EBITDA margin expected to be sustained at around current levels for FY27 and FY28; EPC margins to dilute with scale, offset by product mix.
Peak borrowing for FY27 estimated at around INR130 crore at a cost of about 9%.
BESS and transmission expected to contribute from H2 FY27 and FY28; BESS guidance treated as incremental to the INR600/1,000 crore targets.
capex_capacity: VCBs and RMUs require additional capex; quantum and funding not yet formalised. FPI needs no incremental capex.
Compact FPI at advanced stage, targeted launch in roughly 2-3 months if technology partnership materialises; VCB roll-out may take about a year including type tests; RMU at initial stage.
Transmission entry expected through final-stage tenders; first breakthrough to be announced soon.
BESS: re-entering with small, distributed projects; tenders identified in Rajasthan and Bihar; bids to be submitted shortly.
Management says it is fully resourced for FY27 and FY28 INR1,000 crore target with sanctioned financing in place.
demand_pricing: Order book INR807 crore (ex-GST) at 30 June, ~2.7x FY26 revenue of ~INR300 crore; management cites ~18-24 months visibility, mostly repeat customers.
Q1 fresh awards INR58.37 crore across three states: Bihar PM-Surya Ghar INR56 crore (RESCO), Odisha FPI order (75-day delivery), and Madhya Pradesh FPI order INR3.37 crore with 5 years AMC.

Qualified bid pipeline INR1,350 crore; tenders at final stage exceed INR1,200 crore. Of the INR1,200 crore, ~INR70 crore awarded so far, rest under evaluation, with a 1-2 month wait; management guides 15-20% strike rate.
New-state strike rate ~10-15% vs 30-40% on prior exposure, per management's answer; JV and PSU back-to-back models used where eligibility is not met.
Receivable days are long: management cites ~180 debtor days across the sector; collections improving via TReDS, purchase invoice discounting and surety bonds in place of bank guarantees.
International exploration at an early stage; Africa opportunities being explored, no Sri Lanka opportunity seen.
